approved: Nation-building Funds Repeal (National Disability Insurance Scheme Funding) Bill 2017

The majority voted to agree with the main idea of the bill. In parliamentary jargon, they voted to give the bill a [second reading](https://www.peo.gov.au/learning/fact-sheets/making-a-law.html). ### What is the bill's main idea? The [bill](http://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/r5940) is: > *Part of a package of 11 bills to fund the Commonwealth’s contribution to the National Disability Insurance Scheme ... [and] repeals the [Nation-building Funds Act 2008](https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/Bills_Search_Results/Result?bId=r3099); and makes consequential amendments to five Acts.* That Act established *"three financial asset funds to provide capital investment in transport, communications, energy, water, higher and vocational education and health infrastructure: the Building Australia Fund, the Education Investment Fund and the Health and Hospitals Fund."*

Opposition argued the Nation-building Funds Repeal Bill 2017 closes the Education Investment Fund (EIF) and Building Australia Fund, stripping nearly $4 billion from education infrastructure. The member pointed to EIF-funded projects including $73.8 million for CQUniversity's dual-sector merger, $50 million for the University of Queensland's Advanced Engineering Building, and noted international education exports contribute over $22 billion annually to the Australian economy.
